title: Cyber Crime Branch v. Transnational Digital Arrest Impersonation Syndicate
crime_type: Digital Impersonation / Fake CBI/ED Video Call Coercion / Money Laundering
court_or_authority: Special Cyber Sessions Court, Mumbai / Patiala House Court, Delhi
legal_citation: Cyber Crime FIR No. 312/2023; 2024 SCC OnLine Del 1422
source: Delhi Police IFSO Unit & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 420 IPC (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property)
Section 468 IPC (Forgery for purpose of cheating)
location: New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata & Southeast Asian Cyber Hubs
evidence: Fake police station sets, forged Supreme Court arrest warrants, and counterfeit CBI/ED official letterheads used in Skype/WhatsApp video calls
VoIP call routing metadata demonstrating caller-ID spoofing impersonating central law enforcement offices
Over 200 mule current accounts opened in corporate names utilized to layer and cash out victim deposits within minutes
Testimonies of senior citizens held under continuous 72-hour virtual video surveillance before liquidating life savings
modus_operandi: Contacted elderly victims falsely alleging that parcels in their name containing narcotics and fake passports were seized at customs. Connected victims via video call to fraudsters dressed in authentic police uniforms sitting against official-looking backdrops. Placed victims under continuous digital arrest, threatening imprisonment unless their life savings were transferred to government verification accounts.
personality_disorder: Calculated psychological terrorization, systemic exploitation of fear and respect for state authority.
common_traits: Impersonation of high-ranking IPS officers and judicial judges
Continuous video call surveillance (digital arrest) to isolate victims
Forged Supreme Court and Enforcement Directorate legal notices
High-speed mule account layering to avoid recovery
summary: Landmark prosecution against the digital arrest phenomenon targeting elderly citizens. Triggered nationwide advisories by the Prime Minister Office, MHA Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), and major telecommunications firewall implementations.
